title: Types, Conversion, and Strict Equality
summary: Work with strings, numbers, booleans, null, undefined, explicit conversion, template literals, and strict equality without relying on surprising coercion.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply the JavaScript behavior taught in Types, Conversion, and Strict Equality
Test behavior using observable output and assertions
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: JavaScript values include strings, numbers, booleans, `null`, `undefined`, bigints, symbols, and objects. Browser form values are normally strings. Convert intentionally with `Number`, `parseInt`, or `parseFloat`, then verify `Number.isNaN` when failure matters. The `+` operator concatenates when either operand becomes a string, so explicit conversion protects arithmetic. Prefer `===` and `!==` because they compare without type coercion. Template literals use backticks and `${expression}` for readable output. `null` is an intentional empty value; `undefined` commonly means no value was supplied or assigned.

sections.heading: Guided practice
sections.content:
1. Create a `.js` file.
2. Predict each output.
3. Run it in Node.js or a browser console.
4. Change one value.
5. Explain the observed change.
6. Add an assertion for the intended behavior.
